name: text_cut
note: REVIEW: set by src/phase4/calibrate_search.py on the validation split (300 queries, seed 0, fake wardrobes of 30 Fashion Product pieces): the lowest cut where the best result shown as close is right at least 90% of the time. On the test split it is right 87.2% of the time (reports/phase4/search_calibration.csv). Re-run the script after changing the model or the data. Words are compared with pictures, so the numbers are low.

name: photo_cut
note: REVIEW: set by src/phase4/calibrate_search.py on the validation split (300 queries, seed 0, fake wardrobes of 30 Fashion Product pieces): the lowest cut where the best result shown as close is right at least 90% of the time. On the test split it is right 80.0% of the time (reports/phase4/search_calibration.csv). Re-run the script after changing the model or the data. A picture is compared with pictures, so the numbers are high. This is the less certain cut: with other seeds or more queries it moves and the target is not always reached (labels such as blue / navy or flats / casual shoes look alike), so check it with a larger run (--queries 1000). UPDATE from the encoder lab, Phase 6 (tuning rule commit 1fa3bca): the photo target is now 0.75 (words stays 0.90), and the cuts above (words 0.292, photo 0.792) replace the ones set by calibrate_search.py.

name: target_precision
note: REVIEW: how often the best result shown as close must be right when the cut is chosen on the validation split (calibrate_search.py picks the lowest cut that reaches it).

name: wardrobe_size
note: REVIEW: pieces in each fake wardrobe of the calibration (a typical wardrobe in our survey is small; 30 is the start value).

name: default_limit
note: REVIEW: results returned when the request gives no limit (the request may ask for 1 to 20).

name: closest_anyway
note: REVIEW: when nothing is close, how many of the nearest pieces the app still shows, muted, under 'Closest anyway'.
